pr_title: drivers: Check errors on devices selected using dt macro
pr_body:
Some Kconfig defined devices may be defined using dt_chosen_label
function. Since there is no way to ensure a device enabled in dts
is also defined in Kconfig, it may happen that instance is not
actually defined.
In this case device_get_binding might return 0, leading to undefined
behavior in the function that calls it.
When not already done, systematically check return of function
device_get_binding on devices defined through dt_chosen_label macro.
Trigger ASSERT when required and return error when possible.

Fixes #20068

Signed-off-by: Erwan Gouriou <erwan.gouriou@linaro.org>
pr_comments: @erwango Misspelled subsys? (susbsys). Anyway I don't think subsys should be in the title, so you could remove it.

Even if the initial issue which is dts/Kconfig device instance desynchro that was at the initiation of this issue cannot happen anymore due to recent changes, I think the check is sane and worth keeping.
If this does not go in v2.3.0, I'll close the point so we don't keep it eternally.

issue_context.title: Application doesn't start when SHELL-UART is enabled and UART is not connected on STM32F0
comments:
Hi @victorrsoliveira 

I've tested quickly your sample on `nucleo_f030r8`, and this is still working fine when I'm adding `CONFIG_SHELL=y`.
I don't see what can go wrong, but usual suspect when adding features is pin or peripheral conflict, which is board dependant.

I came here to report the exact same issue, but (un)fortunately found yours instead.

The board I am testing is STM32F091CC, with Shell and Console on USART3, which I manually added to dts_fixup.h and included in my board .dts and Kconfig respectively.
Using GDB I find the board enters arch_system_halt(), reason 0.

Looking at the backtrace, I find that the function *sys_dlist_get(sys_dlist_t *list) in dlist.h tries to remove the node object (sys_dlist_remove), which in my case is NULL, and triggers the fault.

@victorrsoliveira, @jmbrederveld , I've been able to run the proposed piece of code, with provided `prj.conf` on a `nucleo_f091rc`. I am still not getting the reported issue.

Is there any piece of information I am missing to reproduce this issue?

Thank you for investigating. 
Can you please try the shell on an external UART that is not connected ? Any UART other than USART2 (which by default is connected to the ST-Link MCU).
Please disregard this if that is already what you tested.

@jmbrederveld, thanks  for these indications, I've managed to reproduce the issue and found a fix.

Issue lies in `boards/arm/nucleo_f091rc/Kconfig.defconfig` where USART_1 (or X depending on your configuration) is not enabled if UART is enabled

The following fixed the issue on my side:
```
CONFIG_UART_X=y
```

While fixing the bug is easy, we'd need a way not to enter this kind of issue or detect it easily.
I'll think about it this week end.

review_comments: If asserts are not enabled we would give monitor_dev to uart_irq_rx/tx_disable below. Maybe we should do the handling that you did in shell_uart.c in all places that you added the assert?
This was my initial intention, but in functions invoked in `SYS_INIT` macro (like current `bt_monitor_init`), returned values won't be checked AFAIU.

That is strange, seems wierd to have return codes then. But the return would stop you from doing something harmful at least, it could be a null pointer write which would lead to MPU fault or other types of memory errors. And maybe somebody will check the return value in the future :)

> But the return would stop you from doing something harmful at least, it could be a null pointer write which would lead to MPU fault or other types of memory errors. 

I'd rather not do this as this would likely be easily caught by various code analysis scripts, so this would add support follow-up to this PR.

> And maybe somebody will check the return value in the future :)

Or... somebody will require these functions to be void :-)
well I'm just skeptical since the ASSERT might not be enabled. And then the check would simply be skipped an the code continues, so we would end up in undefined behavior anyway.

I agree. ASSERT are disabled by default, but in case one started to debug this kind of things, enabling them would be one of the first step (was mine at least).
Anyway the real solution to this is solving Kconfig/dt desynchro and @galak is working on it.
